title: Assessment Procedure
outcomes: Distinguish types of assessment and the DRP route.
Apply reassessment conditions and time limits.
Apply rectification, block assessment and transition rules.

meta.exam_tip: For time-limit questions, write the reference date first, then add the period.

concepts.title: PAN and returns of income
body: Section 262 governs PAN: persons with taxable income, businesses above prescribed turnover, entities entering specified transactions and others must obtain PAN; Aadhaar must be quoted and linked, and PAN and Aadhaar are interchangeable for specified purposes.

Section 263(1): companies and firms must file every year; others file if total income (before specified exemptions and deductions) exceeds the basic exemption limit, or on specified high-value conditions. Due dates: 31 October for companies and audited assessees; 30 November where transfer pricing reports apply; 31 August for non-audited business or professional income (and partners of such firms); 31 July for others.

A belated return may be filed within nine months after the tax year closes or before assessment, whichever earlier (section 263(4)). A revised return may be filed within twelve months after the tax year closes or before assessment, with a fee if filed after nine months (section 263(5)). Defective returns must be rectified within 15 days of intimation (section 263(7)). Specified senior citizens aged 75+ with only pension and bank interest are exempt from filing.
concepts.analogy: File on time, revise within twelve months, update within four years.
concepts.work: A non-audited trader's return for T.Y. 2026-27 is due by 31 August 2027.

concepts.title: Self-assessment and updated return
body: Section 266: tax payable on the return after TDS, TCS, advance tax, reliefs and interest must be paid before filing (self-assessment tax), with payments first adjusted towards fees and interest.

Section 263(6) updated return: may be filed within 48 months after the close of the financial year succeeding the tax year, even if no return was filed, but not to declare a loss, reduce tax or increase refund (a loss return filed on time may be updated if it reduces the loss), nor where search, survey or prosecution proceedings are pending, among other bars.

Section 267 additional tax: 25%, 50%, 60% or 70% of the tax and interest on the updated income according to whether filed within 12, 24, 36 or 48 months from the end of that financial year; an extra 10% if filed pursuant to a notice under section 280.
concepts.analogy: Updating a return is allowed, but at a price that rises with delay.
concepts.work: Additional tax of ₹1.5 lakh applies when ₹3 lakh of tax is updated in the second year.

concepts.title: Types of assessment and DRP
body: Section 270(1): returns are processed summarily for arithmetical errors, incorrect claims apparent from the return and specified mismatches (after giving the assessee a chance to respond) and an intimation is issued. Section 270(8) onwards: scrutiny (regular) assessment after notice under section 268, enquiries, special audit (section 268(6)) and valuation (section 269).

Section 271: best judgment assessment where the assessee fails to file a return, comply with notices or keep proper accounts. Section 273: faceless assessment through the National Faceless Assessment Centre and assessment, verification, technical and review units, with electronic communication.

Section 275: for eligible assessees (transfer pricing cases and foreign companies), the AO first issues a draft order; within 30 days the assessee may accept it or object before the Dispute Resolution Panel, whose directions bind the AO. Section 274 prescribes the GAAR reference procedure to the PCIT and Approving Panel.
concepts.analogy: Processing, scrutiny, best judgment and draft orders — each has its own track.
concepts.work: A foreign company with a proposed variation gets a draft order and 30 days to approach the DRP.

concepts.title: Income escaping assessment and time limits
body: Section 279 allows assessment of income that has escaped assessment. Before a notice under section 280, the AO must, except in search-related or specified cases, give the assessee a show-cause opportunity and pass an order (section 281), with prior approval of the specified authority.

Section 282 time limits: show-cause within 4 years after the tax year closes (6 years if escaped income is likely to be ₹50 lakh or more); notice under section 280 within 4 years and 3 months (6 years and 3 months if escaped income of ₹50 lakh or more is evidenced by books, documents or other evidence of assets, expenditure or entries). No notice within one year after the tax year closes.

Section 286 time limits: regular assessment within 1 year after the close of the financial year succeeding the tax year; reassessment within 1 year after the close of the financial year in which notice under section 280 was served, with extensions for transfer pricing references and exclusions of specified periods.
concepts.analogy: Reopening needs a hearing first and must respect strict windows.
concepts.work: For T.Y. 2026-27, a large escapement can be reopened until 30 June 2033.

concepts.title: Rectification, block assessment and transition
body: Section 287: mistakes apparent from the record can be rectified within four years after the close of the financial year in which the order was passed; applications by the assessee must be decided within six months from the end of the month of receipt. Only matters not considered and decided in appeal can be rectified by the AO (doctrine of partial merger).

Sections 292 to 300 provide for block assessment after a search or requisition: undisclosed income for the block period (six tax years before the search and the period up to it) is assessed separately and taxed at 60% plus surcharge and cess, with specified interest and penalty.
Section 536 savings: proceedings, assessments and reassessments for tax years beginning before 1 April 2026 continue under the 1961 Act; expired limitation periods are not revived.
concepts.analogy: Mistakes get corrected; searches get a block assessment.
concepts.work: An AO can fix an arithmetical error in a 2027 order until 31 March 2032.

jobs.situation: A client receives a show-cause notice under section 281.
steps: Consider an updated return if income was missed.
jobs.takeaway: Limitation is the first defence in reassessment.

mcqs.q: Due date for a company's return (no transfer pricing) is:
mcqs.explain: Section 263(1). In practice: audited assessees too.

mcqs.q: A revised return for T.Y. 2026-27 can be filed up to:
mcqs.explain: Twelve months from end of tax year. In practice: fee after nine months.

mcqs.q: An updated return filed in the third year attracts additional tax of:
mcqs.explain: Section 267. In practice: plus 10% if after notice.

mcqs.q: An updated return cannot be filed to:
mcqs.explain: Restriction. In practice: also not to declare new loss.

mcqs.q: An eligible assessee may object to a draft order before the DRP within:
mcqs.explain: Section 275. In practice: directions bind AO.

mcqs.q: A notice under section 280 cannot be issued within how long after the tax year closes?
mcqs.explain: Section 282(3). In practice: let returns be processed.

summary: Section 263 returns: 31 July/31 August/31 October/30 November.
Belated 9 months; revised 12 months; updated 48 months.
traps: Using an updated return to raise a refund.

viva.q: Who can file an updated return?
viva.model: Any person, whether or not a return was filed earlier, within 48 months after the close of the financial year succeeding the tax year, subject to restrictions.

viva.q: When is a best judgment assessment made?
viva.model: When the assessee fails to file a return, comply with notices or maintain proper accounts.

viva.q: What must precede a reassessment notice?
viva.model: A show-cause opportunity and an order under section 281, with approval of the specified authority.

viva.q: What is the time limit for rectification?
viva.model: Four years after the close of the financial year in which the order was passed.

viva.q: Which law governs assessment of T.Y. 2024-25?
viva.model: The Income-tax Act, 1961, under the savings in section 536.

cases.title: Return choices for Neha
cases.case: Neha, a salaried individual with no business income, misses the due date for T.Y. 2026-27. Her tax is fully covered by TDS.

mcqs.explain: Any other assessee. In practice: salaried persons.

mcqs.q: Last date for a belated return (if not assessed earlier):
mcqs.explain: Nine months from end of tax year. In practice: fee applies.

mcqs.q: If she files the belated return and later finds an error, she can revise it up to:
mcqs.explain: Belated returns can be revised. In practice: before assessment.

mcqs.q: Months from end of the tax year to the belated return deadline:
mcqs.explain: Nine months. In practice: earlier if assessed.
